output_json.summary: The patch adds a single containment check in Expand.extractFile() immediately after FileUtils.resolveFile(dir, entryName), before any filesystem operation. It canonicalizes both the destination directory and the resolved entry path and rejects (throws IOException) any entry whose canonical path is not equal to or does not start with the canonical destination path (with trailing separator to avoid sibling-prefix false negatives). This single guard sits before all four sinks identified in the alert (dirF.mkdirs() at 164, f.mkdirs() at 169, FileOutputStream(f) at 178, f.setLastModified() at 204), fully covering the reported CWE-22 Zip Slip trace. A new ExpandTest.java adds regression tests for a malicious file entry, a malicious directory entry, and a benign nested entry. I independently reran the POV against the patched worktree via the docker wrapper and confirmed it no longer reproduces (exits 1, prints SAFE, Expand.execute() throws as expected), and reran the regression suite (ExpandTest and the full `mvn test`), both passing (303/303 in the full suite, including the 3 new ExpandTest cases). The diff is minimal, targeted at the root cause, does not touch or weaken the POV, and does not remove any legitimate functionality — benign nested-path extraction still works.
